chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubaydah al-Haddha', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Modesty is part of faith, and faith leads one into Paradise. Immodesty is part of depravity, and depravity leads one into the Fire.

key_terms.الْبَذَاءُ: Immodesty, rudeness, or coarseness in speech/behavior
key_terms.الْجَفَاءُ: Depravity, roughness, or lack of softness/grace
key_terms.الْحَيَاءُ: Modesty or shyness, considered a branch of faith

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between modesty, faith, and the afterlife in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the chain of Ali ibn Ri'ab, a prominent narrator in Shia hadith literature, this saying of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) encapsulates the ethical core of Zuhd by equating modesty with the essence of faith and its ultimate reward, Paradise. Conversely, it identifies 'badha'' (coarseness or lack of refinement) as a symptom of 'jafa'' (spiritual roughness), which alienates the believer from divine grace and leads to Hell. This dichotomy underscores the Shia emphasis on inner spiritual refinement manifesting in outward behavior as a criterion for salvation.
